initiative.title: Video to canvas
initiative.summary: Turn a narrated screen recording into a spatial, source-linked canvas reviewed in the portable HTML viewer; storyboard first, verified scroll joining second.
initiative.next_action: Answer the viewport-selection and test-clip questions, then start M1 when implementation is requested

sources.anchor: First proof; Repository fit; Decide whether to continue

sources.location: OpenCV motion API, FFmpeg showinfo, opencv-python-headless 4.14.0.94, scrollsnap

claims.statement: A narrated recording becomes a canvas explored in space, with every part linked back to its source video moment.
Displayed pixels come from real frames at known times; unobserved areas are never filled and different moments are never blended across text.
Primary case is a narrated product walkthrough over scrolling static content; lecture is second; general video is a research question.
Changed states sit to the right, frequent changes collapse into stacks, motion plays in place, returns are linked, narration sits near its visit, and large regions can be captured.
First version needs no browser instrumentation, cloud service, or new frontend stack; analysis is offline and on request.
The canvas must beat ordinary video and a change-selected storyboard on real tasks, or the simpler view wins.
The portable HTML viewer is the first surface; native SwiftUI waits for proven value.
process_session.py already embeds session data into viewer.html via write_viewer and uses ffmpeg/ffprobe.
Mark images and browser event offsets are not exact frame-exposure times; extract_frame discards actual output time.
No test suite or tracked sample recording; OpenCV is not installed locally; FFmpeg is.

human_questions.question: Is one manual viewport selection per recording acceptable in the first proof?
human_questions.reason: Determines whether automatic content-area detection is in the first slice.

human_questions.question: May the proof use purpose-made short test recordings, or only existing sessions?
human_questions.reason: Determines the strength of real-footage evidence in M3/M4.

shape.appetite: Experiment-sized: storyboard plus verified scroll joining on short recordings in the HTML viewer, enough to decide whether spatial geometry earns its cost.
shape.problem: Ordinary video review hides how much content was traversed, where it changed, and what was said about it.

recommended_shape.summary: Optional offline analyzer writes canvas.json; viewer.html renders a source-linked storyboard first, then tall scroll columns and changed states, with refused joins falling back to storyboard cards.
provisional_choices: OpenCV phase correlation vs scrollsnap reuse

success_moves: Ship the change-selected storyboard first; it is the comparison baseline, the refusal fallback, and a useful result if stitching fails.
Develop joining against synthetic scroll clips cut from tall screenshots with FFmpeg so every offset is known exactly.
Burn a frame counter into synthetic clips to verify click-to-seek lands on the true source frame.
Keep canvas.json as the single seam; absent or mismatched data leaves today's viewer unchanged.
Introduce OpenCV in one milestone, in an optional pinned virtualenv used only by the analyzer.
Freeze thresholds on synthetic fixtures before running real footage.

first_proof.question: Can verified translation joining reconstruct scrolled content accurately with zero false joins, and does a real walkthrough produce a readable tall view?
first_proof.artifact: Synthetic fixture suite plus one 60-90 s real walkthrough rendered in viewer.html.
first_proof.decision_rule: Continue to the value comparison if synthetic p95 error <= 2 px with zero false joins and the real clip yields a readable tall view; otherwise stop at the storyboard.

rabbit_holes: native canvas before value is shown

dependencies.name: OpenCV-headless + NumPy
dependencies.application_seam: join/verify functions inside scripts/analyze_canvas.py producing canvas.json
dependencies.local_proof: Synthetic FFmpeg-cut scroll clips with known offsets in test_canvas.py.
dependencies.live_proof: One or two real disposable walkthrough recordings.
dependencies.rollout: Optional pinned virtualenv; analyzer only runs on request.

first_proof_role.rationale: Joining accuracy is the core uncertainty; it is exercised on synthetic clips with exact ground truth.

dependencies.name: FFmpeg decode timing (showinfo)
dependencies.local_proof: Synthetic clip with burned-in frame counter.
dependencies.live_proof: Spot-check seeks on a real recording.

first_proof_role.rationale: Already installed and used; mapping is verified directly in M1.

failure_injection: generated fixtures: fixed header, cursor, repeated rows, blank gap, fast jump, mid-scroll edit
fast_local_loop.slower_confirmation: Real disposable walkthrough opened in viewer.html.

milestones.title: Source-mapped storyboard in the viewer
milestones.outcome: Change-selected cards in viewer.html seek the shared player to their exact source frame.
milestones.proof: Burned-in counter matches card frame after seek; synthetic change clip yields expected cards.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Useful storyboard; sessions without canvas data unchanged.

milestones.title: Scroll joining proven on synthetic clips
milestones.outcome: Analyzer emits tall columns and changed states with refusals falling back to cards.
milestones.proof: Fixture suite: p95 <= 2 px, zero false joins, refusal on every jump/edit fixture.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Storyboard still works; joining validated offline.

milestones.title: Real walkthrough on the canvas
milestones.outcome: A 60-90 s real clip renders a readable tall view, a changed state, and a refusal card.
milestones.proof: Random click-to-frame checks and seam inspection.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Canvas usable on short real recordings.

milestones.title: Decide whether the canvas earns its cost
milestones.outcome: Recorded go/no-go versus video and storyboard.
milestones.proof: Small rotated task comparison with time, errors, cost, and direct judgment.

history.change: Prior research (intent brief, Pro report, design, proof plan, review) moved from docs/research/video-to-canvas to sources/ and reconciled into a sleuth intent brief.

Four milestones with one new dependency (OpenCV) isolated in M2 and a go/no-go in M4.
